body:
Split out of **#508**'s five-slice re-plan during the Plan pass on 2026-07-26, after two independent cross-vendor plan reviews found the requirement below is normative in proposal 0016 but **owned by no slice**. This is the sixth seam.

## What

The fragment-write path gains an **authorization deadline the D server itself enforces**:

- `ChunkStore::put_fragment` (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:575-577`) carries the write's **authorization instant / deadline** alongside `(id, fragment)`;
- `FragmentPutRequest` (`crates/proto/proto/wyrd/v0/chunk.proto:25-29`) gains the matching **additive** field;
- the gRPC client (`crates/chunkstore-grpc`) sends it and the **D-server service refuses — rather than queues — a write whose deadline has passed**;
- the local/FS store honours the same contract, so the seam means one thing on every implementation;
- a seeded Tier-0 DST case for 0016's own failure-mode row: *"Bound the fragment write with a caller-side timeout only (no server-enforced deadline) → authorize a fragment write, park it in the D server's accept queue past `W_write`, and assert it is refused."*

## Why — a caller-side timeout bounds nothing

0016 is explicit (`docs/design/proposals/draft/0016-multipart-commit-protocol.md:1551-1576`):

> **`W_write` is an end-to-end deadline, not merely a caller timeout** — a caller-side `await` timeout bounds how long the *writer waits*, not when an already-accepted fragment write *takes effect* on the D server, so the bound is only real if the D server enforces it too: the fragment write carries its authorization instant, and the D server **refuses** (rather than queues) a write whose deadline has passed… **That refusal is the implementing slices' obligation** … without it `G_orphan > W_write + δ_clock` bounds nothing, because a write parked in a server queue can land arbitrarily late.

The whole late-fragment safety argument rests on it. `G_orphan > W_write + δ_clock` is what guarantees a fragment authorized under the last live lease lands **strictly before** its position's orphan grace elapses — so the mark is still present and GC never reclaims the evidence before the late fragment is covered by it. With no server-side refusal, a queued write can land after its evidence is gone: an unreferenced, unevidenced fragment, which is 0016 outcome (a).

**This is not the previously-rejected "add a timeout in `core`" finding.** `results/issue_508/review-rejected.md:10` rejected a *duplicate caller-side* timeout on the grounds that the `ChunkStore` implementation already bounds the network (`crates/chunkstore-grpc/src/client.rs:169-190`). That rejection stands and is not reopened. 0016 says a caller-only timeout is **insufficient** — this issue is the *other end*, server-side refusal, which no existing bound provides and which the seam cannot currently express: `put_fragment` takes only `(id, fragment)` and the protobuf carries only ID and bytes.

## Scope

`crates/traits` (the `ChunkStore` seam), `crates/proto` (the additive request field), `crates/chunkstore-grpc` (client send + **server enforcement**), `crates/chunkstore-fs` (same contract locally), and the seeded DST case. Additive and backward-compatible: a request without the field behaves exactly as today, so no existing writer breaks.

## Out of scope

The multipart records and commit protocol (#636); the staged-byte protection class (#637); the S3 verbs (#508); choosing `W_write`'s **value** and the `G_orphan > W_write + δ_clock` margin (#625 owns the windows — this slice ships the *enforcement mechanism* and takes the deadline as a parameter); any file under `docs/design/adr/` or `docs/design/specs/`.

## Ordering

Prerequisite for **#636** (whose staged fragment writes are the first callers that depend on the bound). It edits `crates/traits/src/lib.rs`, which **#634** also edits, so the two are scheduled into different waves.

## Acceptance

- A `put_fragment` whose deadline has already passed is **refused by the D server**, not queued or applied — asserted against the real gRPC service, not only the client.
- A write parked past its deadline in the server's accept path is refused when it is finally processed (the 0016 failure-mode row, as a seeded DST case).
- A request carrying **no** deadline behaves exactly as today (additive-compatibility test).
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

## Reference

Proposal 0016 `:1551-1576` (the end-to-end deadline argument), `:1478` (the `G_orphan > W_write + δ_clock` strict margin), and the failure-mode row at `:1784`. Part of #508 / epic #513.
title: chunkstore: server-enforced fragment authorization deadline (W_write) — additive proto field + D-server refusal
